testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, pressure of at least ____ must build up in both braking systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build up pressure to at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: Service brakes should:

options.text: Only be tested by a trained mechanic.

questions.explanation: Test your service brakes before every trip. This helps you find problems before you need to brake while driving.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and oil that build up in the air storage tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks to remove these materials. Tanks with a manual drain valve should be drained at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should not move more than:
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, set wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check that it does not move more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: A driver can rely on front wheel braking to work:

options.text: Under all conditions, except for snow.

questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works well under all road conditions, including ice. Front wheel skids are unlikely.

questions.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: If your brakes are hot after going down a steep hill, do not use the parking brake. Let them cool first to avoid damage.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Engage and disable the parking brake.
Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
Uncouple and recouple all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: After the system charges, test the warning signal by rapidly pressing and releasing the brake pedal. This releases air from the system. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Friction inside a brake drum is caused when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction forms when brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air pressure pushes out the rod and moves the:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in S-cam brakes, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank prevents air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It stops air from escaping the system if the compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: Some air brake systems use alcohol to:

options.text: Stop ice from forming in air brake valves.
Lubricate parts of the braking system.
Prevent rust on air brake valves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ice from forming in air brake valves.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the braking system to prevent ice from forming.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch that:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light.
Turns off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, pressing the brake pedal moves an electric switch. This switch turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that the ____ turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Before driving, make sure spring brakes turn on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Block the wheels and release air by pressing the brake pedal repeatedly. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve will pop out and spring brakes will turn on.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
Do not work well on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works together with a vehicle's normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease the braking power. ABS only works when the wheels are about to lock.

questions.question: If you use spring brakes while carrying a heavy load, stopping will:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. If spring brakes activate because air pressure is low, your vehicle needs more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: When driving downhill, brake until your speed is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, hold the brake pedal until your speed drops 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: The brakes do not work as well without ABS.

questions.explanation: If the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, jackknifing is less likely. The driver can maintain steering control. If only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing to one side.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls it.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil that builds up. If water and oil accumulate, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What can happen if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times lets air out faster than the compressor can replace it. If pressure gets too low, the air brakes may stop working.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Stop a vehicle from speeding up while going uphill
Stop a vehicle from speeding up while going downhill

questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not be more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle with air brakes should not leak more than 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repair before it can be driven.

questions.question: How do you inspect slack adjusters on S-cam brakes?

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes.
Put on gloves and push in the slack adjusters.
Remove the drum and look inside.
Block the wheels and turn off the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block the wheels and turn off the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, block the wheels, and turn off the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should move no more than about one inch. If it moves more, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes. Other air brake vehicles built on or after March 1, 1998 must also have them.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes working
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure needed to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes working
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the brake lines. This creates a delay of at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes actually start working. This delay is called brake lag.
